findings.why: Sidecar: the placeholder 'shows the form real tags take'. Core's server tag grammar is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,23}$ (local_operator/library/metadata.py:1289 `_normalise_tag_name`, applied by `create_tag`, which the phone's `create_tag_payload` calls). Proven on the real path in audit.log: a throwaway `MetadataStore.create_tag` REFUSES «موضوع-کا-نام» with TagRefused (the route maps it to 422 bad_tag_name and the editor shows 'That tag was not created.') and CREATES 'topic-name'. So the example teaches a form the product cannot save, inside the field beside «شامل کریں». The sidecar's 'a localised example is fine' rests on a premise the server contradicts. `mobile.library.editor.new_tag_placeholder` must be added to `IDENTICAL_BY_DESIGN.<locale>` in src/i18n/__tests__/catalogues.test.ts with a reason, because the 'no shipped value equals English' test (catalogues.test.ts:281-286) fails on a value identical to en. A different ASCII example (e.g. `weekly-notes`) needs no allowlist entry. Same defect in ru, vi and zh-CN (probed); not my bundles.
findings.verified: tools/tagprobe.py: function-level gate + real MetadataStore.create_tag in a temp dir; tools/verify-repl.ts render — both in audit.log

findings.why: Composed-sentence defect against the call site (library-detail.tsx:346-352: a heading completed by the list of conversation titles below it, or by the detail.no_source line). «جن … میں» is the relative half of an Urdu correlative pair and expects its «ان … میں» in a main clause that this heading does not have, so it dangles; the demonstrative «ان گفتگوؤں میں دیکھا گیا» ('seen in these conversations') is complete, points at the list, and matches shipped Hindi 'इन बातचीतों में दिखा'. Oblique plural گفتگوؤں and masculine دیکھا گیا (اثاثہ) unchanged.
findings.verified: tools/verify-repl.ts render in audit.log; call site read at library-detail.tsx:346-352

findings.current: ابھی کوئی ٹیگ نہیں۔ Librarian اثاثے منظم کرتے ہوئے ٹیگ شامل کرتی ہے۔
findings.replacement: ابھی کوئی ٹیگ نہیں۔ Librarian اثاثے منظم کرتے وقت ٹیگ شامل کرتی ہے۔
findings.why: One subject, two genders in one sentence. Core renders the Librarian as feminine ('Librarian عالمی Library منظم رکھتی ہے', wire.settings.librarian.description) and the main verb here is feminine (کرتی ہے), but the conjunctive participle کرتے ہوئے is the masculine(-plural) form; with a feminine subject standard Urdu wants کرتی ہوئی, which reads heavy in a status line. The gender-invariant 'کرتے وقت' ('while/at the time of') removes the clash without rewriting the sentence; meaning, the ۔ and the Latin name are untouched. Sentence 1 is byte-identical to core tui.tags.empty 'ابھی کوئی ٹیگ نہیں۔'
findings.verified: tools/verify-repl.ts render in audit.log; core feminine rendering quoted from the bounded grep in audit.log

findings.current: ایک اثاثے کے لیے ٹیگز کی زیادہ سے زیادہ حد {limit} ہے۔
findings.replacement: ایک اثاثے پر ٹیگز کی حد {limit} ہے۔
findings.why: «زیادہ سے زیادہ حد» says 'maximum limit' — حد already is the ceiling — and «کے لیے» is looser than the پر core uses for the same rule (wire.errors.desktop.library_tag_limit: 'ایک اثاثے پر زیادہ سے زیادہ {max, number} ٹیگز ہو سکتے ہیں۔'). Honest caveat: core's relay.session.tags.limit_hint ships the same doubling in a different sentence, so this is entrenched elsewhere too; polish, not a violation. Grammatical at every {limit}.
